Well, Queen Blister will be very interested to meet you. We had better make sure you do not go anywhere.’ She flashed the royal patterns along her wings and clapped her front claws together. Seven big, strong SeaWings rose up behind the dragonets. Their claws twitched in a way that felt like a threat.

paragraphs.context: I don’t have time to get married. I have to stop the war
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami says no to getting married. She says she has no time because she must stop the war and save the world.
paragraphs.simple: ‘No way!’ Tsunami said, swinging her tail hard. ‘No, no, no.’ A picture of Riptide came into her head. That was silly, because she hardly knew him either. ‘Absolutely not. First of all, I do not have time to get married. I have to stop the war and save the world.’ And maybe also learn how to be queen of the SeaWings. ‘Second of all, that dragon? No, thank you. I would rather have my tail bitten off a little at a time by snapping turtles.’

paragraphs.context: Whirlpool, Tsunami needs lessons in Aquatic. Can you believe she never learned it
paragraphs.mainIdea: Queen Coral says Tsunami needs lessons in Aquatic. Her face looks kind, but Tsunami wonders angrily if her flashing stripes say something different to the Council.
paragraphs.simple: ‘That reminds me,’ said the queen. ‘Whirlpool, Tsunami needs lessons in Aquatic. Can you believe she never learned it, poor thing?’ She tapped her claws on the stone in front of her. ‘Such a sad way to grow up.’ Her face looked sorry for Tsunami, but her stripes were flashing. Tsunami angrily wondered if the queen was saying something different to the Council, because she knew Tsunami could not understand.

paragraphs.context: Giant wings smashed Tsunami to the rock floor of the tunnel
paragraphs.mainIdea: Someone attacks Tsunami in a tunnel and puts a hood over her snout so she cannot see. The attacker is bigger and heavier than she is.
paragraphs.simple: Giant wings smashed Tsunami onto the rock floor of the tunnel. She tried to twist around, but her attacker kicked her in the head. Then the attacker pushed a hood that smelled of seaweed over her snout, so she could not see. Tsunami shouted and fought, hitting out with her claws and tail. The attacker was bigger and heavier than she was, so she could hardly move under the weight. It seemed that he or she was wearing something to be heavier. She felt something made of metal hit against her spines with a clank.

paragraphs.context: Dragon eggs took a year to hatch, so there should have been clutches
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami sees many nests but no new eggs. She feels guilty because she thinks it is because Gill is gone.
paragraphs.simple: Nests made of seaweed were tucked into small hollow spaces in the floor, with wide paths between them. Dragon eggs took a year to hatch. So there should have been groups of eggs at different stages, from just laid to almost hatched. But there were no new eggs to be seen. Tsunami thought, with a stab of guilt, that it was because Gill had been gone. And he was not coming back.

paragraphs.context: Tsunami pressed the egg to her chest and followed her mother
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami holds the egg and follows her mother, Queen Coral, up through the palace to the top.
paragraphs.simple: Queen Coral tried flashing some more questions at Tsunami. At last she flapped her wings and pointed up to the surface. Tsunami held the egg to her chest and followed her mother. They went up and up and up through winding tunnels and huge palace rooms. They went through coral set with emeralds and curtains of golden sea grass with pearls in them. They swam to the top of the palace. A guard stood watch there over a view that went for miles under the water.

paragraphs.context: Tsunami flapped over to the pavilion and landed next to a large cauldron
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami finds four guards playing a game. By their guilty faces, she guesses they were not supposed to leave the cave.
paragraphs.simple: Tsunami flapped over to the pavilion and landed next to a large pot that bubbled and smelled like green tea. Four guards were sitting close together around a low table. They were playing a game that used rolling fish bones. They all froze when they heard her claws land. Slowly they turned toward her. By their guilty faces she guessed they were not supposed to leave the cave.

paragraphs.context: Tsunami paused, realizing how much they didn’t know
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami says Queen Coral is not like that and that she loves her daughters. Then she tells her friends about the Council, the scrolls, a dragon who tried to kill her, and Tortoise.
paragraphs.simple: ‘Stop it!’ Tsunami gripped her head. It could not be true. ‘She is not like that. She loves her daughters. When she found the other egg broken...’ Tsunami stopped. She saw how much her friends did not know. She went back and told them all about the Council and her mother’s scrolls. She told them about the strange dragon who had tried to kill her in the tunnel. She told them how Queen Coral had acted when Tortoise failed her.

paragraphs.context: you can’t always trust rumors and propaganda, especially when it comes to a big
paragraphs.mainIdea: Blister says the dragonets have probably heard things about her, but they should not always trust rumors. She tells them to ask her anything and hopes they will choose her.
paragraphs.simple: ‘I am sure you have heard things about me too,’ Blister said, going back to Queen Coral’s side. Her tail slid across the cave floor like a snake, and the poison tip made a rattling sound on the stone. ‘But you cannot always trust rumors and propaganda, most of all with a big duty like the prophecy. So ask me anything you like. I would be very happy to help you make your choice, although of course I hope you will choose me.’ Her shining eyes moved over all of them again and back to Coral. ‘So, Coral, what is for breakfast?’

paragraphs.context: Webs pressed on, his wings drooping
paragraphs.mainIdea: Webs says he remembered Tsunami’s egg because it was so blue. He says he did it for the prophecy and for peace.
paragraphs.simple: ‘I remembered her egg,’ Webs went on, with his wings hanging down. ‘It was so blue. It had to be the right one. I am so sorry, Your Majesty,’ he said quickly. ‘But the prophecy is so important. I would never have betrayed you for anything else, but for peace... how could I not do what the Talons asked?’

paragraphs.context: The princess murders started two years before they stole Tsunami’s egg
paragraphs.mainIdea: Starflight says the idea does not work. The princess murders began two years before the Talons stole the egg, and Webs has been underground with them for six years.
paragraphs.simple: ‘Even so, I am not sure that idea works,’ Starflight said. He looked into the air in a vague way, as if he was trying to solve a math problem. ‘The princess murders began two years before they stole Tsunami’s egg. So the Talons, and most of all Webs, could not have known then that they would steal a royal egg. Webs did not even know he would be a Talon then. And Webs has been underground with us for the last six years. He could not have flown here and back every time he wanted to murder a dragonet.’

paragraphs.context: She braced the spear against the floor, and the statue’s chest slammed into it
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami fights the statue with a spear. She sees bits of dark green stone break off it.
paragraphs.simple: The statue jumped straight at her. She held the spear firmly against the floor, and the statue’s chest hit it. A hard, shaking shock ran through Tsunami’s claws, as if she had been stabbed in both palms. The statue bounced back, and Tsunami saw bits of dark green stone break away and fall into the water. She thought, maybe it can be smashed into little pieces.

paragraphs.context: Orca carved that statue and dedicated it to the hatchery
paragraphs.mainIdea: Queen Coral says the statue told them that Orca put a spell on it. She thinks Orca made it to get rid of dragons who might come after her or fight her.
paragraphs.simple: Coral shook her head. ‘Before we destroyed it, Anemone made the statue come alive again and made it tell us who had put a spell on it. It said Orca, as clear as day.’ She sighed again. ‘Orca made that statue and gave it to the hatchery a short time before she challenged me. I think she expected to win. So she was getting ready a way to get rid of dragons who might take her place or fight her.’

paragraphs.context: It felt like leaping into a freezing hailstorm, icy drops pelting her snout
paragraphs.mainIdea: Tsunami jumps at a wall of water. The icy drops hit her cracked ribs, but she lands on solid rock.
paragraphs.simple: She took a deep breath, spun around and jumped at the wall of water. It felt like jumping into a freezing storm of hail. Icy drops hit her nose and closed eyes. They cut into her gills through the seaweed bandage. They hammered the broken places in her ribs. She got ready for pain as sharp as lightning. But a moment later her claws landed on solid rock.

paragraphs.context: Clay went next, spreading his wings to shield Sunny and Starflight
paragraphs.mainIdea: As the dragonets leave, a SkyWing turns toward them. Tsunami fights her, but the SkyWing kicks back and Tsunami’s cracked ribs hurt. Then the SkyWing breathes fire at Clay’s back.
paragraphs.simple: Clay went next. He spread his wings to shield Sunny and Starflight. A SkyWing in the battle saw them and turned fast toward them. Tsunami jumped at her, grabbed her nose and kicked her belly as hard as she could. The SkyWing kicked her back, and bright lines of pain went along Tsunami’s cracked ribs. Tsunami lost her hold. The SkyWing roared out a blast of fire at Clay’s back as he left.

paragraphs.context: She’s gotten all squeamish about animus powers since finding out about her first daughter
paragraphs.mainIdea: Blister says Queen Coral is hiding in the Deep Palace, where Blister cannot get to her. Blister says it has not been her favorite week of the war.
paragraphs.simple: ‘And both her brats as well,’ said Blister. ‘It would not be helpful for me if she died.’ She showed her teeth and hissed softly. ‘Of course, now she is hiding in her Deep Palace where I cannot get to her. And she says firmly that my secret weapon will be no use to me for years still. She has become nervous and uncomfortable about animus powers since she found out about her first daughter. She would rather waste the little one’s magic just to stop her from turning into a killer.’ Blister sighed out a small burst of flame. ‘It has not been my favorite week of the war.’

sentences.context: they’d already wasted a day flying south of the Diamond Spray Delta
sentences.simple: In Tsunami’s view, they had already wasted a day flying south of the Diamond Spray Delta. This was mostly because Starflight worried and complained until everyone agreed.
sentences.grammar: ‘they’d wasted’ is ‘they had wasted’ (past perfect): the day was already lost before the moment Tsunami is thinking about. ‘As far as Tsunami was concerned’ means ‘in Tsunami’s opinion’.

sentences.context: it had taken an entire day for it to occur to him
sentences.simple: She also loved that it took him a whole day to think of the fact that the Kingdom of the Sea was underwater.
sentences.grammar: ‘It occurred to him that...’ means ‘the thought came into his mind’. ‘It had taken an entire day for it to occur to him’ is past perfect: the long wait came before this moment. ‘It takes (time) for ... to ...’ tells how long.

sentences.context: especially with a full-grown dragon weighing them down
sentences.simple: The current had carried them farther away than Tsunami had guessed. It was very hard to swim back to the beach, most of all with a full-grown dragon making them heavy.
sentences.grammar: ‘with + noun + -ing’ (‘with a dragon weighing them down’) gives a reason or condition that is true at the same time. ‘Weigh down’ means ‘make heavy’, and ‘especially’ stresses that this made it worse.

sentences.context: only taking him by surprise had given her a temporary advantage
sentences.simple: He was too big and too strong for her up there. Only surprising him had given her a short time of being ahead.
sentences.grammar: ‘Only taking him by surprise’ is an -ing phrase used as the subject; ‘take someone by surprise’ means ‘surprise them’. ‘had given’ is past perfect: the advantage came earlier than the moment now.

sentences.context: a dream in which their cave had collapsed and was slowly crushing her
sentences.simple: She woke up suddenly from a dream. In the dream, their cave had fallen down and was slowly crushing her to death.
sentences.grammar: ‘in which’ means ‘in the dream’ and starts a clause that describes it. ‘had collapsed’ is past perfect (the cave fell first), and ‘was crushing’ is past continuous (an action going on over time).

sentences.context: If it was a shark, she would kill it and bring it back
sentences.simple: If it was a shark, she would kill it and bring it back to the others to eat. She would do it mainly to see the look on Starflight’s face.
sentences.grammar: ‘If it was ..., she would ...’ is a second conditional: it imagines a situation and says what she would do. ‘so she could see’ tells the purpose.

sentences.context: as if she were a dead eel someone had left half-eaten
sentences.simple: His eyes, which made her feel uneasy, looked her over from her wing tips to her claws, as if she were a dead eel that someone had left half-eaten on the beach.
sentences.grammar: ‘as if she were’ uses ‘were’ for something not real: it only seems that way. ‘someone had left’ has no ‘that’: it is a clause that tells which eel, and ‘had left’ is past perfect (earlier).

sentences.context: gone before the bubbles of their splash had cleared
sentences.simple: Then, one by one, half the guards around them dived into the same spot. Each one disappeared the same way, gone before the bubbles from their splash had cleared.
sentences.grammar: ‘gone before the bubbles ... had cleared’ uses ‘before’ + past perfect: the guards were already gone while the bubbles were still there. It shows how fast they moved.

sentences.context: It didn’t look like it had been built; it looked as if it had
sentences.simple: It did not look as if someone had built it. It looked as if it had grown that way, although Tsunami was pretty sure that was not possible.
sentences.grammar: ‘it had been built’ is passive past perfect (someone made it earlier). ‘looked as if it had grown’ says how it seemed, and ‘although’ adds a thought that goes against it.

sentences.context: as if his wings had barely been strong enough to carry him
sentences.simple: Starflight arrived last. He caught hold of the side and fell forward, as if his wings had hardly been strong enough to carry him.
sentences.grammar: ‘as if’ + past perfect (‘had been’) says how it seemed: his wings looked too weak. ‘barely’ means ‘almost not’, and ‘strong enough to + verb’ means strong enough for that job.

sentences.context: then giving him back once everyone had escaped
sentences.simple: Most of the tribe hid in their secret place and acted mysterious and powerful but not helpful. But Morrowseer kept turning up. He told them the dragonet prophecy, looked the dragonets over, tried to get Glory killed, and saved Starflight (but no one else) from the SkyWings. Then he gave Starflight back once everyone had escaped.
sentences.grammar: ‘kept turning up’ means ‘kept appearing’, and the -ing words after it (delivering, inspecting, trying, saving, giving) list what he did. ‘once everyone had escaped’ uses past perfect: the escape finished first.

sentences.context: wondered grumpily if that was really why Queen Coral had forbidden SeaWings
sentences.simple: Anemone looked a little like the dolphins they had seen earlier. Tsunami wondered, in a bad mood, if that was really why Queen Coral had said SeaWings could not eat dolphins.
sentences.grammar: ‘wondered if that was really why ...’ is an indirect question. ‘had forbidden’ is past perfect (the rule came before Tsunami’s thought), and ‘forbid someone to + verb’ means to order them not to do it.

sentences.context: Glory could spit a deadly venom, which seemed to be a RainWing skill
sentences.simple: In the SkyWing palace, they had found out that Glory could spit a deadly poison. This seemed to be a RainWing skill that most dragons did not know about.
sentences.grammar: The ‘which’ clause adds a comment about the whole idea before it. ‘they’d discovered’ is ‘they had discovered’ (past perfect): it was before now. ‘could spit’ means ‘was able to spit’.

sentences.context: that looked like ancient stone ruins: palaces and temples that had collapsed long ago
sentences.simple: They swam for what felt like miles over wide parts of coral reef covered with algae. The reef looked like old stone ruins, like palaces and temples that had fallen down long ago.
sentences.grammar: ‘that looked like ancient stone ruins’ is a clause that describes the reef. The colon introduces examples (palaces and temples). ‘that had collapsed’ describes them, and ‘had collapsed’ is past perfect.

sentences.context: now the cavern was lit only by trails of glowing jellyfish
sentences.simple: Now the cave was lit only by lines of glowing jellyfish in the water below.
sentences.grammar: ‘was lit’ is passive: the jellyfish gave the light. ‘only by’ means there was no other light. ‘trails of’ means ‘lines of’.

sentences.context: a wild, brief moment of thinking Anemone had been about to kill her
sentences.simple: For a short, wild moment she thought that Anemone was about to kill her.
sentences.grammar: ‘had been about to + verb’ means ‘was going to’, seen from a later time: she thought Anemone was just about to kill her. ‘moment of thinking’ is noun + of + -ing.

sentences.context: After the way her friends had been looking at her lately
sentences.simple: Her friends had been looking at her in a way that showed they did not trust her. Because of that, Tsunami did not want to risk the same kind of reaction from her mother.
sentences.grammar: ‘had been looking’ is past perfect continuous: the looking went on up to that time. ‘After the way ...’ means ‘because of how ...’, and ‘lately’ means ‘recently’.

sentences.context: Tsunami had loved the look on Queen Scarlet’s face when she broke
sentences.simple: But when she did it, the truth was that Tsunami had loved the look on Queen Scarlet’s face when she broke Gill’s neck.
sentences.grammar: ‘the truth was ...’ introduces something she does not want to admit. ‘had loved’ is past perfect: she felt that way at the earlier moment she is remembering.

sentences.context: who looked at her as if he didn’t see a future queen
sentences.simple: He looked at her as if he did not see a future queen or a father killer, but only a dragon he liked very much.
sentences.grammar: The ‘who’ clause tells more about the SeaWing. ‘as if he didn’t see ... anything but ...’ means it seemed he saw only a dragon he liked. ‘whom’ is the object form of ‘who’.

sentences.context: if she’d known it would be a memorial one day
sentences.simple: Tsunami wondered if Queen Coral’s first daughter had carved a picture of herself, and if she had known it would be a memorial one day.
sentences.grammar: ‘wondered if she’d known’ is an indirect question; ‘she’d known’ is ‘she had known’ (past perfect). ‘would be ... one day’ looks forward to the future from a point in the past.

sentences.context: didn’t really think the ridiculous dragon could have overpowered her for a moment
sentences.simple: Whirlpool did not look as if he had been in a fight. And Tsunami did not really think that silly dragon could have beaten her, even for a moment.
sentences.grammar: ‘could have + past participle’ talks about a past possibility; with ‘didn’t think’ she believes it was not possible. ‘as if he’d been in a fight’ uses past perfect after ‘as if’.

sentences.context: big enough to eat a dragonet the size of Anemone, she guessed
sentences.simple: The sharks were bigger than Tsunami had expected. She guessed they were big enough to eat a dragonet as big as Anemone.
sentences.grammar: ‘bigger than Tsunami had expected’ compares, and ‘had expected’ is past perfect (the expecting was earlier). ‘big enough to + verb’ means big enough for that action. ‘she guessed’ shows it is not a fact.

sentences.context: these two were about to get swamped and end up at the bottom
sentences.simple: She wondered if they could breathe underwater or swim, because these two were about to be covered by the sea and end up at the bottom of the ocean.
sentences.grammar: ‘were about to’ means it was going to happen very soon. ‘get swamped’ is a passive made with ‘get’ (to be covered by water). ‘end up’ means ‘finally be in a place’, and ‘because’ gives the reason.

sentences.context: how the queen would react when she found out Tsunami had sauntered
sentences.simple: Tsunami could not tell if the guards felt guilty about leaving her friends to drown too, or if they were only worried about what the queen would do when she learned that Tsunami had calmly walked right into the dragonets’ cave.
sentences.grammar: ‘couldn’t tell if A or if B’ gives two possibilities. ‘how the queen would react’ is a noun clause, and ‘would’ looks forward from a past time. ‘had sauntered’ is past perfect: it happened before the queen finds out.

sentences.context: she’d been a little worried that the little SandWing might still be too mad
sentences.simple: Tsunami had been a little worried that Sunny, the little SandWing, might still be too angry with her to want to help.
sentences.grammar: ‘she’d been worried’ is ‘she had been worried’ (past perfect): the worry came before she felt glad. The ‘that’ clause says what she feared. ‘too mad ... to want’ means ‘so mad that she would not want’.

sentences.context: the mysterious dragon who’d tried to kill her in the tunnel
sentences.simple: Tsunami told them about the strange dragon who had tried to kill her in the tunnel.
sentences.grammar: The ‘who’ clause tells which dragon. ‘who’d tried’ is ‘who had tried’ (past perfect): the attack came before she told her friends. It is one item in a list joined by commas and ‘and’.

sentences.context: the way Queen Coral had reacted when Tortoise failed her
sentences.simple: She also told them how Queen Coral had acted when Tortoise failed her.
sentences.grammar: ‘the way’ + clause means ‘how’. ‘had reacted’ is past perfect: it happened before Tsunami told them. ‘when Tortoise failed her’ gives the time.

sentences.context: with Shark in the dungeon, even for only a day or two
sentences.simple: Also, with Shark in the dungeon, even for only a day or two, Tsunami felt that she, her friends and the egg would all be a lot safer.
sentences.grammar: ‘with Shark in the dungeon’ (with + noun + place) tells the situation. ‘would be a lot safer’ uses ‘would’ for a result she expects. ‘Not only that, but ...’ adds one more good point.

sentences.context: it was enchanted to kill only when it was sure no guards
sentences.simple: She guessed that a spell made it kill only when it was sure no guards were around: no queen, and no one to see what it did and stop it from attacking again.
sentences.grammar: ‘was enchanted’ is passive (someone put a spell on it). ‘to kill’ tells what the spell was for, and ‘only when’ limits the time. ‘She guessed’ shows it is an idea, not a fact.

sentences.context: if she tried to carry the egg with her, the statue could crash down
sentences.simple: If she tried to take the egg with her, the statue could crash down on both of them and break the egg easily.
sentences.grammar: ‘if she tried ..., the statue could ...’ is a conditional about a possible danger; ‘could’ means ‘might’. The -ing phrase ‘shattering it easily’ tells the result.

sentences.context: Anemone reanimated the statue and made it reveal who had enchanted it
sentences.simple: Before we destroyed the statue, Anemone made it come alive again and made it tell us who had put a spell on it.
sentences.grammar: ‘made it reveal’ is ‘make + object + verb’ and means ‘forced it to tell’. ‘who had enchanted it’ is a noun clause, and past perfect shows the spell came before the telling.

sentences.context: was overpowered and dragged off to the same prison cave where Riptide and Webs
sentences.simple: One by one, each dragonet was overpowered and dragged off to the same prison cave. Riptide and Webs had disappeared there the day before.
sentences.grammar: ‘was overpowered and dragged off’ is passive (done to the dragonets); ‘overpower’ means ‘beat by force’. The ‘where’ clause tells the place, and ‘had disappeared’ is past perfect (before the dragging).

sentences.context: if they’re mad or hungry, they’re probably giving off shocks pretty frequently
sentences.simple: If they are angry or hungry, they probably give off shocks quite often.
sentences.grammar: ‘If they’re ..., they’re probably giving off ...’ talks about a real possible situation. ‘give off’ is a phrasal verb that means ‘send out’, and ‘pretty’ here means ‘quite’.

sentences.context: If she could get to it without the guards noticing
sentences.simple: If she could get to the chain without the guards noticing, and then move the mechanism without the guards hearing it, Riptide and Webs would be free to escape with the dragonets.
sentences.grammar: ‘If she could ..., ... would be free’ is a second conditional: a plan and its possible result. ‘without + noun + -ing’ (‘without the guards noticing’) means ‘while the guards do not notice’.

sentences.context: now it would be her fault if Anemone became Blister’s pawn
sentences.simple: Instead, now it would be her fault if Anemone became Blister’s pawn, a person for Blister to use.
sentences.grammar: ‘would be ... if ... became’ is a conditional that imagines a bad result. ‘instead’ shows the result is the opposite of what Tsunami wanted.

sentences.context: What were the chances a scout had spotted the hole, reported back
sentences.simple: How likely was it that a scout had seen the hole, told the others, and gathered soldiers for an attack only a day later?
sentences.grammar: ‘What were the chances ...?’ is a question that means ‘it was very unlikely’. ‘had spotted, reported back, gathered’ are past perfect steps that came before the attack, joined by commas and ‘and’.

sentences.context: version of Pyrrhia where they could have grown up as a family
sentences.simple: She wondered if there was any version of Pyrrhia where she, Coral, Gill, Anemone and Auklet could have grown up as a family, normal and happy, with no one trying to kill anyone.
sentences.grammar: ‘could have grown up’ imagines a different past that did not happen. The ‘where’ clause tells which Pyrrhia, and ‘with no one trying ...’ is ‘with + noun + -ing’ and tells the condition.

think of.meaning: To have an idea come into your mind, or to remember or consider something.

point out.meaning: To say something so that people notice it.
point out.example: They’d know it was her,” Glory pointed out.

burst out.meaning: To come out of a place suddenly and with force. It can also mean to say something suddenly.
burst out.example: Clay immediately burst out of their cave

listen to.meaning: To pay attention to what someone says or to a sound.
listen to.example: too mad at her right now to listen to sense

go on.meaning: To keep talking or doing something; to continue.

get out.example: We have to get out of here

hold out.meaning: To stretch out your arm, hand or claw in front of you.

look for.example: dive in and look for the SeaWing palace

stand up.meaning: To get up onto your feet. It can also mean to point straight up.
stand up.example: Whirlpool puffed out his chest and stood up.

come on.meaning: Words you say to ask someone to hurry, to follow you, or to try harder.

as soon as.example: As soon as they hit the water, Tsunami swam

step back.example: Tsunami stepped back, curling her claws around the keys

let out.meaning: To make a sound, a breath or a cry come out of you.
let out.example: Shark let out a long hissing breath.

take care of.meaning: To look after someone or something, or to do what is needed for them.
take care of.example: I’ve managed to take care of myself up to now

wake up.example: Tsunami finally woke up on an island

find out.meaning: To learn a fact that you did not know.
find out.example: I found out I was stolen from the Royal Hatchery

one by one.meaning: One after the other, not all at the same time.
one by one.example: One by one, each of the dragons followed her.

let go.example: She let go and so did Clay.

pick up.meaning: To take hold of something and lift it.
pick up.example: picked up a large conch shell

run away.meaning: To leave a place or a person quickly, to escape.
run away.example: He ran away during a battle

keep up.meaning: To move as fast as someone else so that you stay with them.
keep up.example: She flapped her wings frantically, trying to keep up.

get rid of.meaning: To remove something or someone that you do not want.
get rid of.example: I’ll get rid of this Council

hang on.example: trying to hang on to the heavier, larger dragon

catch up.meaning: To reach someone who is ahead of you.
catch up.example: She beat her wings to catch up

come true.meaning: To happen in the way that someone wished or hoped.
come true.example: believing in the prophecy, wanting it to come true

set off.meaning: To start going on a trip or toward a place. It can also mean to make something start.
set off.example: set off for it in a frantic paddle

fall asleep.example: The rest of them fell asleep halfway into it

be about to.meaning: To be ready to do something very soon.
be about to.example: He was about to call out to the others.
